instance_recommendations.rationale: AMD-based variant of c5 with identical vCPU/memory specs at 10.4% lower cost. Direct drop-in replacement for c5.2xlarge with no architecture change (x86_64). Best cost-per-instance option available.

Newer-generation AMD instance with slightly better price-performance than c5a. Nearly identical pricing to c5a.2xlarge but with improved compute from 3rd Gen AMD EPYC processors. Good alternative if c5a capacity is limited in your AZ.
Current baseline instance type. No savings but zero migration risk. Keep as fallback in a mixed-instance policy if preferred alternatives have insufficient capacity.

rationale.scaling_policy: The policy was redesigned around the observed queue depth distribution. The median queue depth is ~1,043 messages and the average is ~1,850, so scale-up thresholds were raised compared to the current policy to avoid premature provisioning. Scale-down is triggered aggressively: below 50 messages (near-empty queue) removes up to 40 instances, 50-200 removes 15, and 200-500 removes 5, ensuring rapid de-provisioning when demand drops. Scale-up begins only above 500 messages (well below the median) with a modest +5, increasing through higher thresholds aligned to p50 (1,500), p95 (~5,600 mapped to the 3,500-7,000 band), and p99 (~8,400 in the 7,000-15,000 band). The top two steps handle burst scenarios up to and beyond the observed max of ~43,000. Fewer aggressive scale-up steps and higher thresholds reduce instance churn and over-provisioning, accepting slightly higher queue latency during ramp-up in exchange for significant cost savings.
rationale.strategy_impact: Cost optimization strategy drove several decisions: (1) Cooldown set to 300s (matching the instance_drain_seconds maximum) which slows both scale-up and scale-down reactions—this prevents rapid oscillation and reduces wasted partial-hour billing from short-lived instances. (2) Scale-down adjustments are large and start at low queue depths to shed capacity quickly when demand falls. (3) Scale-up thresholds are raised (first scale-up at 500 vs. the current 150) so the ASG tolerates moderate queue backlogs before adding instances, reducing average fleet size. (4) c5a.2xlarge recommended as primary instance type, saving ~10.4% per instance with identical specs. At the average fleet size of ~53 instances, switching to c5a.2xlarge saves approximately $1,702/month (~$20,400/year). (5) Reduced scale-up aggressiveness across the board means lower peak instance counts during moderate demand spikes.
rationale.risk_notes: 1) The 300s cooldown applies to both scale-up and scale-down; during sudden traffic spikes the ASG may take longer to reach adequate capacity, temporarily increasing queue latency. The observed max desired of ~160 instances and max queue depth of ~43K suggest infrequent but significant bursts that may queue longer under this policy. 2) The aggressive scale-down step of -40 when queue < 50 could cause rapid capacity drops; the min_size of 1 provides a safety floor, but re-scaling after an aggressive scale-down will take multiple cooldown cycles. 3) c5a.2xlarge uses AMD EPYC processors—verify that the Celery beautify workload has no Intel-specific optimizations (e.g., AVX-512 or MKL dependencies). 4) Zero-depth percentage is only 1.39%, meaning the queue is almost always occupied; this validates keeping min_size at 1 rather than 0. 5) Max capacity should remain at 250 as observed peak desired was ~160, leaving headroom for growth.
